name: Catbalogan Watershed Forest Reserve
legalBasis: Proclamation No. 413, s. 1994 (signed 29 June 1994 by President Fidel V. Ramos)
administeringAgency: DENR, through the Forest Management Bureau, in coordination with other government agencies (Proclamation No. 413)
statedPurpose: Protecting, maintaining and improving water yield; maintaining usefulness as a source of potable water, for irrigation, domestic use and other forestry purposes (Proclamation No. 413)
administrativeCoverage: Municipalities of Catbalogan and Jiabong, Province of Western Samar, as stated in the 1994 proclamation
source: Proclamation No. 413, s. 1994: legal technical description of the reserve
dataset: Legal technical description: 53-corner bearing/distance traverse tied to Barangay Boundary Monument (BBM) No. 13
feature: Catbalogan Watershed Forest Reserve, corners 1 to 53
sourceGeoreference: Tie point BBM No. 13 at latitude 11°48'31.6" N, longitude 124°53'29.8" E. The proclamation does not state the geodetic datum; the coordinates are used as published and are not transformed.
geometryDerivation: Generated by tools/technical-description-to-geojson.mjs. Corner 1 = published tie point; each later corner is solved from the published bearing and distance (Vincenty direct, WGS 84). The ring is closed on corner 1. No digitising, simplification or manual editing.
areaMethod: Stated: 804.9 ha (Proclamation No. 413). Calculated: 804.93 ha, ellipsoidal area of the GeoJSON ring on WGS 84 (equal-area). Plane-traverse area from the bearings and distances: 804.90 ha. Discrepancy +0.03 ha (0.004%).
traverseClosure: Misclosure 1.60 m over a 12,113 m perimeter (1:7,585), within ordinary cadastral-survey tolerance. The geometry and the stated area are internally consistent.
positionalAccuracy: Shape and area follow the legal description exactly. Absolute position is NOT survey-verified because the tie-point datum is unstated (pre-PRS92 coordinates can differ from WGS 84 by up to a few hundred metres). Cross-check: corner 45 ("a point along Salug River") lies 104 m from the OpenStreetMap-mapped Antiao River, and the plotted reserve contains the mapped upper Antiao River. Treat the position as approximately ±100-200 m.
digitalDatasetsSearched: DENR Forest Management Bureau ArcGIS (fmbfsd.denr.gov.ph), FSD_Portal layer 0 'WS_PROC - Proclaimed Watersheds': no Catbalogan entry and nothing under Proclamation 413. Region VIII lists Palompon, Anas, Jicontol, Hinabian-Lawigan, Pan-as and Hayiban only. Retrieved 2026-10-06.
DENR FMB critical watersheds (Critical_Watershed_MIL1), redelineated watersheds (Feb 2025) and forest-land layers: none represents this reserve.
World Database on Protected Areas (UNEP-WCMC ArcGIS service): no Catbalogan site.
OpenStreetMap: only an unofficial point 'Catbalogan Water Catchment' (node 3002232001); no polygon.
Geoportal Philippines: no public query service for this reserve was found.

verification.identity: Verified: official name, designation, legal basis and municipalities taken from the text of Proclamation No. 413, s. 1994.
verification.geometry: Verified against the legal description: 53 of 53 legs parsed, closure 1:7,585, computed area matches the stated 804.9 ha. Valid simple polygon with no self-intersections.
verification.position: Approximate: tie-point datum unstated; see positionalAccuracy.

notes: Real GIS STUDY AREA / watershed management context only. It is NOT the operational contributing catchment: the runoff model keeps the simulated 0.30 km² catchment until Phase 2B delineates the actual drainage area to the modelled outlet from an elevation model. The 3D terrain, rivers, reservoir, pumps, roads and service areas remain schematic and simulated. If DENR releases an official digital boundary, it supersedes this plotted geometry.
